chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Al-Walid ibn Uqba Al-Hajariy, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, a believing servant will not insist upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding his need, except that He fulfills it for him.'

key_terms.إِلْحَاحٌ: Insistence or persistent asking in supplication

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of insisting in supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on supplication, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the spiritual principle of 'ilhah' (earnest persistence), where a believer’s unwavering focus on their need demonstrates deep conviction. Shia scholars interpret this not merely as a guarantee of immediate fulfillment, but as a reflection of Allah’s responsiveness to sincere, persistent devotion, often linking it to the concept of awaiting the divine response with patience.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, from Al Waleed Bin Uqba Al Hajariy who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘By Allahazwj! A Momin servant will not insist upon Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic regarding his needs except Heazwj would Fulfil it for him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sayf ibn ‘ Amirah from Muhammad ibn Marwan from al-Walid ibn ‘Uqbah al-Hajari who has said the following: “I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘By Allah, if a believing servant (of Allah) insists before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, on praying and pleading before Allah for help. He will fulfill his needs.’”
